Grab some dinner and a pint while enjoying our long-running Old-Time Jam! Featuring many talented musicians from the local WNC area, our traditional Appalachian mountain music jam runs from 5-9pm every Wednesday night at Jack of the Wood! Jack Of The Wood is still a downtown hot spot for food, brews and drink since 1997 and founders Joan and Joe Eckert who still own it, have maintained the original lively English and Irish vibe. The old-time mountain and Irish music jams continue, including a hot bluegrass jam Thursdays and brunch every Sunday. item.description: The Queen Sessions at Hotel Eve | A celebration of the legendary women who shaped jazz. As the bandleader and vocalist of Queen Bee and the Honeylovers, Whitney Moore Roda has spent years immersed in the jazz and swing traditions of the 1930s and ’40s. Ella Fitzgerald has been a particular inspiration, not only for her extraordinary voice and groundbreaking improvisation, but for the playfulness and spontaneity she brought to every performance. In this tribute, Whitney celebrates the original Queen of swing with a selection of favorites from the Great American Songbook. Trumpeter Justin Ray joins her to revisit some of the iconic duets of Ella Fitzgerald and Louis Armstrong, with Taylor Pierson on piano and Trevor Stoia on bass rounding out the quartet. $10 weekdays -$15 weekends at the door (all ticket proceeds are 100% passed to the band, backed by a living wage guarantee from Hotel Eve) *Reserve a table in advance, or join us impromptu the night of the show. item.description:
Awakening Asheville ### **Walking in Balance**
*Finding Harmony Within Ourselves and Our Relationships*
As the seasons change and the days grow shorter, nature reminds us that life is always seeking balance. There are times to give and times to receive. Times to speak and times to listen. Times to hold on—and times to let go. But in the busyness of everyday life, it is easy to lose that balance.
We may give so much to others that we neglect ourselves. We may hold onto responsibilities, expectations, relationships, or old stories long after they have become too heavy to carry.
This New Moon invites us to pause and ask: **Where in my life am I being called back into balance?**
Join us for our monthly sacred virtual New Moon gathering as we step away from the noise of everyday life and create space to listen within. item.description:
Crokinole Tuesdays at Highland Brewing Taproom Join us every Tuesday in the Taproom for an evening of flicks, strategy, and friendly competition! We’re hosting the Asheville Crokinole Club—a community of players who love this classic dexterity board game. Never played? No problem! Crokinole is easy to learn and endlessly fun. Players take turns flicking wooden discs across a circular board, aiming for the high-scoring center zones. The twist? If your opponent has discs on the board, you must hit one—miss, and your piece is out! Whether you’re a seasoned pro or just curious, come grab a pint, meet new friends, and test your skills.

item.description: Hit the trails and learn more about The North Carolina Arboretum’s botanically diverse forest with a guided trail walk! April through October, this free hiking program is led by trained volunteer guides who take small groups of participants along woodland trails and through a variety of forest types. Depending on the season and each guide’s area of expertise, topics of discussion may include wildflowers, plant and tree identification, natural history and more. Guided trail walks are limited to 15 people, including the guide, and are not recommended for guests under 16 years of age. Groups depart from the Baker Visitor Center Lobby on Tuesdays at 1 p.m. and Saturdays at 10 a.m. and 1 p.m.. Walks last 1.5 – 2.5 hours, are approximately one to two miles in length. As this program is held rain or shine, all participants should dress appropriately for the weather. There is no pre-registration; walks are first-come first served and sign up sheets are located in the Baker Visitors Center.

item.title: The Sound of America — Thu Nov 12, 7:00 PM — Asheville Art Museum
item.description: AmiciMusic returns with a thrilling program entitled “THE SOUND of AMERICA.” Pianist and Artistic Director Daniel Weiser will be joined by violinist Tim Schwarz from Philadelphia in this exciting exploration of the incredible diversity of our American sound. The program includes Spirituals and Ragtime as well as Blues-inspired works by W.C. Handy and William Grant Still, the Native-American inspirations of Charles Cadman, the Jewish influence on Ernest Bloch, the country fiddling in Aaron Copland, and the Latin rhythms in Bernstein’s West Side Story. Weiser and Schwarz served as the 1996 U.S. Artistic Ambassadors of Music for which they performed more than 50 concerts in 11 countries in the Middle East and Southeast Asia showcasing our American music. AmiciMusic is a chamber music organization based in Asheville and Baltimore dedicated to performing the highest quality chamber music in intimate venues and non-traditional spaces.
